problem:
A body of mass $6\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)={t}^{3}-{t}^{2}$ meters per second.
Find an expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $\sqrt{2}\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$  At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡t$ meters per second. 

Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ seconds. Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the force equals
{{field-1}} $\text{N}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sec}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =ma(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F(\frac{\pi }{4})|=|2|=2\,\text{N}.
$$
